changes: The remembered MICRO T value now lives with the module. A power cycle clears it, and the row starts on grid again.
Offsets already written on the trigs stay in the pattern.
On a unit, a power cycle brought the MICRO T footer back to on grid.

First Modwerk catalog release: TRACK TRIG EDIT gains MICRO T under TRIGS. LEVEL rewrites every step on the selected audio or MIDI track through the stock micro-timing writer. Remembered row lives in module bss (mt_table, 2048 bytes); loader clear and power-cycle drop the unit so the row starts on grid. USB package ABI 7, 2926 B, module 36200ffc, sha256 8958a66f2942e4e0c5692c0cf075bab3c07e4f3347d716ac57405b1792cb6c47. Keep Accept + power-cycle footer reported 18 November 2026 on title-variant package f5b9682175f295875dbecb66a18524c205ba526d88e9bd7dc9cdd7d270d01292 (ColdFire image identical). ot_emu measured 788 instructions/event; memory total 3188 bytes. No battery RAM.
TRACK TRIG EDIT gains MICRO T under TRIGS. The window still shows four rows, so REC.TRG scrolls into view.
Turn LEVEL on that row and every step on the selected track takes that micro timing, in the stock fraction.
MIDI button off writes the audio track. MIDI button on writes the MIDI track and leaves the audio track alone.
The footer shows the fraction. The lane keeps dashes, a centre 0, and a cursor. The remembered number lasts until power-off.
Documentation only: TRACK TRIG EDIT is the declared screen. One byte per bank, the pattern on the screen, and track; audio and MIDI share it. Still a draft.
